about.metaDesc: How the service works and the technical bits
about.subtitle: How it works, on purpose
about.intro: ModrinthProxy is a **platform** to find and download Minecraft mods. Thousands of mods, plugins, shaders and the rest in one place, with a Russian-first UI.
about.catDesc: Open-source data, structured. We collect mod metadata and show it in a usable shape.
about.linksDesc: We don’t store mod files. Links go to the authors’ official sources.
about.uiDesc: Translated UI, navigation, categories — built for Russian-speaking users first.
about.filterDesc: Filters for Russian law. Blocked content is dropped automatically.
about.aggregator: We’re an **information aggregator** — we collect mod data and make it easy to reach. Files live on authors’ servers; we only give links and descriptions. You get original files from the people who made them.
about.legalNote: This is for rights holders and users: we are independent of official Modrinth and Rinth, Inc. We respect trademarks and use them only to name the service we talk to.
about.step1d: You search for a mod, plugin or shader on this site
about.step2d: The system finds the data in the databases
about.step3d: A direct link to the author’s official file
about.middle: Technically we’re a **middle hop** between you and the data sources. Russian UI, plus content filters.
about.dlNote: **Note:** Download links go to the authors’ servers. Ours never touch the files — we only serve information.
about.lawLead: We try to follow Russian law and filter content:
about.blockProjects: **Project blocks:** Projects with banned content are dropped from search and can’t be opened.
about.blockImages: **Image filters:** Images with banned symbols are swapped for a blank placeholder.
about.blockText: **Text replace:** Banned terms in titles and descriptions are replaced with neutral characters.
about.blockOrgs: **Org blocks:** Projects from some organizations can be locked down.
about.projectsHint: Individual mods, plugins, shaders, resource packs, data packs and modpacks with banned content. Hidden from search and catalog; their pages are locked.
about.orgsHint: Authors and teams whose whole catalog is hidden. Counted separately from single blocked projects.
about.mediaHint: Images with banned symbols: avatars, icons, gallery shots, description images. Replaced with a blank placeholder.
about.autoFilters: Filters run automatically on our server. Block lists get updated as the law requires.
about.contactLead: This email is **only for official requests** from state bodies (Roskomnadzor, prosecutors, courts and other authorized structures) about blocks and filters.
about.contactNote: Don’t use it for author appeals, ads, or anything unofficial. Those messages get ignored.
about.nextDesc: React framework with SSR. Server Components and Actions.
about.ossDesc: Source is open on GitHub if you want to read it or contribute.
about.cloudDesc: Runs on a modern cloud so the site stays up and pages load.
about.ddosLead: The site is shielded from DDoS and similar attacks by **mitelis.net**. That’s how we keep it up and pages fast.

bot.metaTitle: Scan mods and plugins for hacks and backdoors — JAR analysis | ModrinthProxy
bot.metaDesc: Free pre-install scan of mods and plugins: 150+ static Java bytecode rules, a report of almost everything the file can do. The .jar body is not stored — hash only for repeats. Optional deep AI pass. Telegram. Separate resource-pack unpack tool for developers.
bot.ogTitle: Scan mods and plugins for hacks and backdoors — JAR analysis
bot.ogDesc: Free. 150+ Java checks, report before you install. Files are not kept. Telegram.
bot.h1: Scan mods and plugins for hacks
bot.intro: Before you put a plugin on a server or a mod on your PC, check the file for malware, spyware, hidden network calls and extra commands. The pipeline is **150+ Java bytecode checks**: the bot returns **almost the full range** of what that mod or plugin can do on your machine or server — before you install it.
bot.service: The scan service — free, focused on your file’s safety
bot.freeD: No payment, no “pay to scan” gate. Anyone who opens the bot can use it.
bot.noStoreD: After analysis the original isn’t sitting on disk for a stranger. Repeats of the same build only keep a hash — you can’t rebuild the archive from it.
bot.reportD: Not a single “clean/dirty” line. Hits and priority: network, perms, commands, classes, methods — **150+ Java bytecode checks** make a dense picture. Then jdec or a neural net if you need more.
bot.deepNote: “Deep research” that sends slices of suspicious code to OpenAI is opt-in — details below. The main line runs on our infra.
bot.jarP1: Same format for client and server: Java inside the archive can call the internet without you, poke player perms, drag extra APIs and classes. The bot runs a static pipeline of **150+ Java rules** and builds a report so you see **almost the full range of what the file can claim**: malware/spyware hooks, network and command patterns, what to re-check by hand before install. Not an antivirus percentage and not a courtroom in chat — a risk snapshot before you put an unverified build on prod or your PC.
bot.jarP2: How: open the bot from the link at the bottom, send the **original .jar as a document** (not a screenshot, not “files as pictures” — the file). It unpacks, runs rules, replies with findings; a second send of the same build can be faster via the stored **hash**, without keeping the archive body.
bot.chat: What the chat report looks like
bot.chatP1: One message. Top: archive name, size, classes scanned, rule hits, two scales — **“safe”** and **“check this”**: some hits are legit (metrics, configs, the loader), some actually need a read. Below: **file hash (xxHash64)**; same file next time can match without storing contents.
bot.chatP2: Each detail block is a warning (console commands, internet, addons folder, reflection, file ops, Base encodings, dynamic class load, SpigotMC license strings, etc.), then a class path like pkg/ClassName.class and methods like execute, split by a line. Easy to paste into jdec or a neural net for one spot in the code.
bot.chatP3: The same message can add a support contact for questions about the report — look at the bottom of the Telegram screen after the full dump.
bot.sample:
💾 JAR ExamplePlugin.jar
📏 Size 115.4 KB
📋 Classes scanned: 66
⚠️ Rule hits: 10
   │ Safe: 8
   │ Check this: 2
🔐 File hash (xxHash64): a9a6fb988524d0b8

⚠️ File can run commands as console.
🚩 Class: pkg/SomeFeature.class
⚙️ Method: execute, execute
━━━━━━━━━━
⚠️ File connects to websites.
🚩 Class: pkg/metrics/Sender.class
⚙️ Method: sendData
━━━━━━━━━━
💬 Questions? @…
bot.sampleNote: Live builds can have a lot more blocks: the same rule can fire in different classes and methods — the report tries to list them so you decide from plugin context.
bot.deepLead: Extra .jar analysis with a neural net — when the base checks aren’t enough.
bot.nnD: Uses **GPT from OpenAI** on slices of suspicious code.
bot.how1: Some checks can trigger deep research.
bot.how2: Suspicious fragments go to the net for a closer read.
bot.how3: You get a longer explanation of the risk.
bot.goes: What can go to the net
bot.goes2: commands and permission work in a plugin or mod.
bot.settings: In **bot settings** you can turn deep research on or off. For max caution leave it on if you’re willing to send selected suspicious slices to OpenAI as described.
bot.policyLead: We don’t keep your file contents after the scan and nobody can download them as an archive.
bot.p1: Files aren’t stored on the server — deleted after the scan, no outside access to contents.
bot.p2: Repeats of the same file only keep a **hash** (checksum). You can’t rebuild the jar from it.
bot.p3: The report is priority-ordered: worst hits first.
bot.p4: Main analysis runs on our infra. Separately: with deep research on, selected suspicious slices go to OpenAI as above.
bot.confused: If you don’t get the result
bot.confused1: The bot flags suspicious classes and methods, e.g. “connects to websites” with class and method names.
bot.confused2: Open the .jar in **jdec.app** and read those spots. If Java isn’t your thing — paste the method into any net you have (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude, …) and ask what the code does.
bot.tgAria: Open the JAR scan bot in Telegram
bot.rpD: Not part of the hack scan. Separate content tool: e.g. a Minecraft pack from a server locked by Praxelis or IA — when you can’t pull textures out, the bot can repack the file. Enable the “Resource pack” module in settings and send the pack as a document.
bot.why: Why scan mods and plugins for hacks
bot.why1: A .jar from a catalog can look fine and still do anything a Java program can: hidden outbound requests, commands as admin, leaking data from the server or the player’s machine. For Minecraft mods (Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, Quilt, …) and server plugins (Bukkit-family cores, hybrids) the risk is the same — the environment you drop the file into.
bot.why2: No mod repo fully guarantees a build isn’t malware or just against your server policy: authors change, builds get rebuilt, mirrors show up. **Scan the jar for hacks and typical backdoor patterns** — you see signals (network, perms, weird classes) before players or your box eat it.
bot.why3: On Modrinth, content is reviewed **only before first publish**. On update **that review does not run again**: the new .jar doesn’t get the same human pass — leftover is automation, reports, and mods reacting, with errors and delays. A long-lived project is not a reason to trust the latest zip without your own scan: run every archive, especially after an update.
